neighbours.label: word or word piece right after a negation (un- prefix or 'no'/'not'), esp. ' time' in 'wasted no time'/'not enough time' and stems like un-god-ly, unse-em-ly, unsur-prisingly, not improbable
fire: When the doors opened, the eager shoppers wasted no time grabbing the discounted televisions.
The new coach wasted no time in reshaping the team's defensive strategy.
Our manager said the project would not get enough time to be tested properly.
She woke at an ungodly hour to catch the first ferry to the island.
Such public bickering between ministers was considered deeply unseemly by the press.
Unsurprisingly, the cheapest hotel in town was fully booked for the festival.
It is not improbable that the letter was written by a later copyist.
Investors wasted no time selling their shares after the scandal broke.
quiet: The shoppers spent a long afternoon browsing the electronics aisle downstairs.
The new coach slowly reshaped the team's defensive strategy over the season.
We had a wonderful time at the beach with our cousins last summer.
She woke at six o'clock to catch the first ferry to the island.
Such public bickering between ministers was widely reported by the press.
As expected, the cheapest hotel in town was fully booked for the festival.
It is likely that the letter was written by a later copyist.
What time does the museum open on Sunday mornings?

notes: Label and sentences written blind by a Claude subagent from the card text alone (prompt: haiku_labeler/prompt.md, identical for Haiku, Sonnet and Opus); one retry on mechanical checks. Part of a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus comparison on the same 48 poles.
